Battle of Vorontsovka — A military clash between the Caucasian Islamic Army and German troops in Georgia.
Background
The Ottoman state was working to sign separate treaties of friendship and cooperation with Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan. Turkey wanted to control some strategic regions and railways in order to conduct its military operations in the Caucasus safely, and to ensure that Armenian and Georgian forces would not be able to interfere with Turkish military operations. The Germans strongly opposed these demands, which the Turks tried to convince the Georgians and Armenians to accept. The Germans took control of the Batumi-Tbilisi ​​railway with the Georgians in Poti. Not satisfied with this, the Germans began to form units from their soldiers who had been captured by the Russians.The Armenians wanted to give control of the Tiflis-Culfa railway to the Germans. The Ottoman state quickly completed the necessary work in the face of these changes and accepted their wishes. On May 31, 1918, it signed treaties of friendship and cooperation with the Armenians in Batumi, and on June 3, 1918, with the Georgians.
This innovation did not delay in opening the gap between Germany and the Ottoman state. The deputy commander-in-chief Enver Pasha went to Batumi with the German general Von Seeckt, the chief of staff of the Ottoman armies, to resolve some of the misunderstandings that had arisen between Turkey and Germany. The issue was thoroughly investigated here.
Battle
The commander of the 3rd Army, Wahib Pasha, ordered the Turkish troops in Gyumri to advance on Tbilisi The troops, which began their advance on 10 June 1918, routed the combined Georgian-German forces that came their way. They also captured some German officers and soldiers.
This was the only battle in World War I in which the Allies fought each other.
Result
As a result of the intervention of the German headquarters under Enver Pasha, the prisoners were released, and the Turkish army stopped its advance. Despite these changes, the Germans continued to create various obstacles to the Turkish army's use of the railways in Georgia.
Wahib Pasha was removed from office.
